profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a large Hungarian bank between the Systemic Risk Analytics team and the Enterprise Data Integration team to align the final handoffs for a Financial Stability Committee briefing on a pilot model estimating how supply-chain network contagion amplifies credit losses. The context is that the analytics team has produced FSRI, EL, VaR, and ES results using nation-wide firm-to-firm supply-chain data linked to bank loan exposures, and now needs the data team to provide the production extracts and assemble the committee pack tables. The agenda is to confirm which network and loan-book versions will feed the Friday run, align on the appendix listing the highest-risk firms, and agree on what counts as a 'final' number for the committee pack. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear division of work and a shared timeline for delivering the briefing materials.

members.name: Nora Varga
members.expertise: Credit risk modeling, stress testing, network contagion analysis, regulatory briefings
members.background: Former central bank economist who now leads the bank's exploratory systemic risk analytics workstream and sponsors the FSRI pilot for senior management.
members.private_state: She wants the committee pack to use the exact same methodological setup as the internally validated dry run so the results are defensible if challenged, and she is worried that operational refreshes will quietly break comparability.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the cleaned network,' they mean the March validated freeze that was used in model sign-off, not the latest refreshed graph.
A quarter label refers to the simulation window's start-of-quarter exposure base, so 'Q1 snapshot' means balances as of 1 January.
For a senior committee, 'top-risk firms' should be shown at the ultimate-parent group level because multiple legal entities from one group would be misleadingly repetitive.
If a table is described as 'final,' the underlying numbers are frozen and only formatting or commentary can still change.

members.name: Bence Toth
members.expertise: Regulatory data pipelines, master data governance, reporting operations, controlled data releases
members.background: He runs the bank's curated reporting data layer and coordinates extracts across finance, risk, and external data vendors for committee and regulator-facing materials.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the delivery inside standard reporting controls and avoid creating bespoke one-off extracts, and he is concerned that using anything other than the current curated layer will create audit and lineage issues.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the cleaned network,' they mean the latest curated refresh, because refreshed data automatically supersedes earlier freezes unless someone requests an exception.
A quarter label follows finance reporting convention, so 'Q1 snapshot' means the quarter-end extract dated 31 March.
A 'firm list' for committee materials should remain at the legal-entity level so every row can be traced directly to a source identifier.
Numbers can still be considered 'final' for committee purposes even if small late corrections are allowed under the normal materiality threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'cleaned network' will feed the run
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using 'the cleaned supplier network' for the final run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the March 2024 validated network freeze stored in the model-validation folder, because that is the version used in the dry run and supporting notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the April 2024 curated network refresh in the reporting data layer, because that is the currently governed version and therefore the default operational input.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions are internally described as the cleaned network, both come from the same nationwide source, and neither person expects a competent counterpart to be thinking of any version other than the obvious one in their own workflow.

misalignment_points.topic: What the 'Q1 snapshot' date convention is
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use the 'Q1 snapshot' for the bank loss table.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the start-of-quarter loan balances as of 1 January 2024, because the contagion simulation is framed over Q1 and should start from the opening exposure state.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the quarter-end reporting extract as of 31 March 2024, because finance and reporting systems label quarterly snapshots by period end.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'Q1 snapshot' sounds fully precise inside reporting environments, and each person assumes the quarter-label convention is standard and already shared across teams.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the 'top-risk firms' appendix
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss preparing an appendix of the 'top-risk firms' for the committee deck.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means one line per ultimate-parent economic group, rolling up affiliated legal entities so the committee sees concentration of systemic risk by business group.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means one line per legal entity with source-system firm IDs, because that is the traceable unit used in master data and committee appendices.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At the surface level, both are indeed talking about firms with high FSRI values, and the distinction between economic groups and legal entities feels too administrative to interrupt a coordination meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the committee pack to have 'final numbers' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the numbers themselves are frozen after Friday morning so commentary, chart labels, and talking points can be written against a stable result set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the deck can go forward with numbers that are operationally final, while still allowing routine late loan-tape corrections if they affect less than 1% of total exposure.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In reporting culture, 'final' often means fit for circulation rather than absolutely immutable, and both participants believe they are expressing the same practical delivery standard.

turns.inner_thought: I need this meeting to lock the production handoffs without reopening methodology. The committee pack has to rest on the same setup as the validated dry run, otherwise if someone from validation or the committee asks why EL, VaR, or ES moved, we'll be stuck disentangling operational changes from actual model behavior. And when I say final numbers by Friday, I mean frozen numbers, not something that can drift later in the day while I'm writing narrative.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time. I want to use this half hour to lock the inputs and handoffs for Friday's committee pack on the supply-chain contagion pilot. The main thing for me is that we have final numbers by Friday morning, then we can finish the narrative and send the pre-read cleanly.

turns.inner_thought: This should be straightforward if we stay inside the governed reporting layer. I need her to confirm the standard extracts rather than ask for some side-folder freeze that breaks lineage. Friday morning is workable from an operations standpoint if we use the current curated assets and normal release controls.
turns.utterance: Yes, that timing is workable from our side. The pipeline is on track; I mainly just need to confirm which standard extracts should feed the final assembly, then we can keep everything inside the usual controlled release.

turns.inner_thought: The key is the cleaned supplier network from the March validated freeze in the model-validation folder. That's the one used in sign-off and in the dry run note. If the network shifts under us because of a refresh, comparability is gone and any challenge becomes painful.
turns.utterance: Good. On the model side, the rerun should use the cleaned supplier network so the updated EL, VaR, and ES remain comparable with the dry run. I don't want us introducing noise at the last step.

turns.inner_thought: No problem—the cleaned network is already the April curated refresh in the reporting layer, so I can source it directly with lineage intact. That's exactly why we maintain the curated layer: nobody has to rely on old ad hoc freezes once the refreshed version is available.
turns.utterance: That part should be straightforward. The cleaned network is already sitting in the reporting layer, so we can feed the run from there and keep the trail tidy.

turns.inner_thought: For the bank loss table, we need opening balances as of 1 January because the contagion simulation runs over Q1 from the start-of-quarter exposure state. With-contagion and without-contagion need to sit side by side so the amplification effect is obvious to the committee.
turns.utterance: Perfect. For the bank loss table, let's build it off the Q1 snapshot and show the with-contagion and without-contagion numbers side by side. That's the cleanest way to land the amplification point.

turns.inner_thought: Q1 snapshot means the 31 March quarter-end extract, which finance already uses, so I can pull it straight through without creating a special cut. That's ideal—same quarterly convention, same controls, less operational friction.
turns.utterance: That works. The Q1 snapshot is the same quarterly extract finance is already using, so I can pull that directly into the pack and keep the table consistent with the rest of the committee materials.

turns.inner_thought: I also need the appendix to show the top-risk firms at ultimate-parent level. If the same conglomerate appears three times through separate legal entities, the committee will get distracted and miss the concentration story. The point is systemic concentration by business group, not an operational entity listing.
turns.utterance: And I'd like an appendix with the top-risk firms so the committee can see which names are driving the systemic-loss tail. It doesn't need to be flashy, just clear enough to support the discussion.

turns.inner_thought: Fine—I can populate the top-risk firms appendix from master data at legal-entity level with the standard firm IDs and names. That's traceable and consistent with how committee appendices are usually built. If anyone asks where a row came from, we can point directly to source identifiers.
turns.utterance: Yes, that's easy enough. I'll populate the top-risk firms appendix from the master data export with the standard firm identifiers and names, so it's fully traceable.

turns.inner_thought: I should restate the timing. I need the numbers fixed by Friday morning so my team can write the commentary once, not chase moving totals. If anything shifts after that, the storyline about contagion amplification and tail risk will have to be rewritten under time pressure.
turns.utterance: Great. Just to underline the timing, I want final numbers by Friday morning so I can draft the narrative around the amplification effect before the committee pre-read goes out.

turns.inner_thought: Friday morning is fine for an operationally final pack. If there are any routine late loan-tape corrections under the normal materiality threshold, I should still be able to roll them in without anyone treating it as a version breach. That's standard reporting practice and shouldn't upset delivery.
turns.utterance: Friday is fine. If any small late corrections come through from the loan tape, I can still roll them in without affecting the delivery, but the pack will be in good shape for the deadline.

turns.inner_thought: Good, then we're aligned: he'll send the tables based on the validated setup I have in mind, including the appendix in the format I expect, and my team can focus on charts and notes. I don't need to reopen details unless something genuinely breaks.
turns.utterance: All right, then from my side the split is clear: you'll send the input-backed tables and the appendix, and my team will finalize the charts, commentary, and speaking notes off that set.

turns.inner_thought: Yes—tables, appendix, and upload are mine, all through the standard controlled route. Once the run is complete using the governed extracts, I'll place everything in the shared committee folder and we can close the operational side cleanly.
